title: Identifying Localized Pressure Loss: Clogged Faucet Aerator
description: When low water pressure occurs at a single faucet while the rest of the building has normal flow, the problem is usually isolated to that specific fixture. Water supply lines carry small particles of mineral scale and sediment over time. These particles become trapped behind the fine mesh screen of the faucet aerator attached to the spout tip. As debris accumulates, it restricts water flow rate without affecting system pressure elsewhere. Unscrewing the aerator housing, rinsing the screen, and checking the rubber washer often restores full flow quickly. Does your building experience localized or system-wide pressure loss?
image_prompt: A macro educational photograph in a vertical 9:16 aspect ratio, focusing on a disassembled kitchen faucet spout tip resting on a clean countertop near a sink. The chrome-plated brass aerator housing is unscrewed, clearly displaying the fine stainless steel mesh screen filled with realistic calcium sediment, mineral grit, and tiny rust particles blocking the mesh openings. Beside the metal housing, the dark rubber sealing washer and internal plastic flow restrictor core are neatly laid out in physical order. Clean professional lighting from the side highlights the texture of the sediment particles and metallic threads. The central plumbing assembly is sharp and centered, leaving clean blurred background area at the top and bottom third for text overlays. No text, no logos, no watermarks, photorealistic detail, physically realistic plumbing components.
visual_story: The visual focuses on the physical mechanism of localized flow restriction. By showing the disassembled aerator components and highlighting the mineral sediment trapped directly against the fine mesh screen, the viewer immediately sees why water flow drops at a single fixture. The clear separation of parts (housing, screen, washer) visually demonstrates how easy it is to inspect this point of restriction before assuming there is a main line issue.

on_image_text.hook: Low pressure at just one faucet?
on_image_text.explanation: Mineral sediment and rust particles collect against the fine mesh screen inside the aerator, restricting fixture flow.
on_image_text.takeaway: Inspect and clean fixture aerators before adjusting main supply valves.
